paragraphs: Rav Idi bar Avin Naggara (see there). His wife was a priest’s daughter, Ellu Overin 49a; he ate on account of his wife, Chullin 132a. His brother was Rabbi Chiyya. Two sons fit for ordination descended from him, Rabbi Sheshet (some places Rabbi Shisha) and Rabbi Yehoshua. The Gemara asks, “Actually ordained—could you think so?” Perhaps ordination had ceased in their time, or he was in Babylonia and had not gone to the Land of Israel. Rather, they were fit for ordination. He instituted a practice in Naresh. He sent before Abaye, Bava Batra 32b; spoke to Abaye, Bava Metzia 35b; Mo'ed Katan 16a. Abaye spoke to him, Chullin 97b; Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua (see there). He sat before Rav Chisda and told him, “A baraita agrees with you,” Arvei Pesachim 101b. In Rav Chisda’s name, Eruvin 59b; Bava Metzia 4a. He came for judgment before Rav Chisda and said, etc. Rav Chisda said, “Is this the man they call great? On whom does the master rely—on this one?”, etc. (His sitting before him, coming for judgment before him, and reporting in his name apparently show he was Rav Chisda’s student. Rav Chisda called him “master,” disproving the rule that a teacher does not call his student “master.”) Bava Batra 33a. He told Rav Chisda, “Thus I recite it in bar Hinuk’s baraita”; see there. Keritot 21a: Adda b.A. In Rav Yehudah’s name in Rav’s name, Yevamot 85a. In Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, Keitzad Me'abberin; Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ashyan’s name. Rabbi Nechemyah bar Barukh in his name. In Rav Amram’s name. His locality was Hintzevu; Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua came there, and he called them “children,” Yevamot 85a; Pesachim, chapter 2, 35a. They likewise came to his son’s house, Shabbat 136a. He objected to Rav Pappa, Chullin 131a. This seems to contradict the earlier writers’ rule that “he asked him” means he was his teacher: how could he call him “children”? He recited in the civil-law collection of Karna’s school. Rava bar Ihi spoke to him; Rabbah, his son. Rav Idi bar Avin said in Rav Amram’s name in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name; see there. Yuchasin writes, in the chronological order of amoraim, seventh generation: “Dorot Olam writes Rav Idi bar Avin was head after Meremar. I do not know who he is. If the man in Rav Chisda’s days, it would be nearly two hundred years; rather, there are two.” End quotation. See part I, 4192: he held office twenty years.
